job.title: Under 16 Head Coach
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Academy Coaching

Reporting to: Youth Development Phase Manager

Closing Date For Applications: 10th August 2026

About the Role:

The Under 16 Head Coach is responsible for leading the coaching, performance and development programme for Nottingham Forest's Under 16 squad, creating an outstanding learning environment that prepares players for the successful transition into full-time football within the Professional Development Phase.

The post-holder will lead the planning, delivery and review of all aspects of the Under 16 football programme, ensuring coaching sessions, match preparation, fixtures and individual player development are fully aligned to the Club's coaching philosophy, playing identity and long-term player development strategy.

As the final age group within the Youth Development Phase, the role plays a critical part in preparing players for a scholarship programme and the demands of the Professional Development Phase. Working under the leadership of the Youth Development Phase Manager, the successful candidate will work in close collaboration with the Professional Development Phase Manager & Under 18 Head Coach to ensure every player's transition is planned, purposeful and centred around their individual development needs.

The role will also maintain a strong collaborative relationship with the Head of Football Development, ensuring player progression, succession planning and transition decisions remain aligned to the Academy's overall football strategy.

The successful candidate will create a demanding, innovative and player-centred environment that develops technically excellent, tactically intelligent and psychologically resilient players capable of thriving within Nottingham Forest's full-time development programme.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

Under 16 Head Coach Responsibilities

  • Lead and manage all aspects of the Under 16 football programme, ensuring the highest standards of coaching, preparation, performance and player development.

  • Plan, prepare, deliver and review all Under 16 training sessions, fixtures and competitive matches in line with the Club's coaching philosophy, playing identity and Academy methodology. Inclusive of training sessions on all three of our training models.

  • Create an innovative, demanding and enjoyable learning environment where players are challenged daily to maximise their long-term potential.

  • Develop players technically, tactically, physically, psychologically and socially in preparation for scholarship and full-time football.

  • Lead all Under 16 matchday activity, including squad selection, tactical preparation, in-game coaching and post-match review.

  • Embed the Academy's coaching methodology and playing principles into every aspect of the Under 16 programme.

  • Prepare players to meet the behavioural, physical, tactical and psychological expectations of the Professional Development Phase.

  • Foster professionalism, resilience, independence and accountability as players prepare to enter the next stage of the Academy pathway.

  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required by the Head of Academy, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy.

  • Ensure all information relating to the individual players performance clock and relevant team information is up to date daily on the Football iP platform.

  • Contribute to the Academy audit preparation ensuring all documentation is recorded and accurately keep up to date on a daily basis.

Player Development & Transition

  • Take a leading role in preparing players for transition into the Professional Development Phase, ensuring every player is equipped to thrive within a full-time training environment.

  • Work closely with the Youth Development Phase Manager to review player progress, establish development priorities and agree appropriate player movement.

  • Develop an outstanding working relationship with the Professional Development Phase Manager & Under 18 Head Coach to ensure seamless transition of players into the Under 18 programme.

  • Collaboratively identify players who are ready to experience the Professional Development Phase through selected training sessions, fixtures and specialist development opportunities.

  • Contribute to scholarship recommendations, transition planning and succession planning across both phases.

  • Ensure all player movement between the Under 16s and Under 18s is supported by a clear developmental rationale and aligned to the player's Individual Development Plan.

  • Maintain regular dialogue with the Head of Football Development regarding players approaching scholarship, ensuring alignment with the Academy's long-term player pathway.

  • Liaise with the Head of Academy on recommendations for player scholarship offers through a strategic process of selection.

  • Assist the Youth Development Phase Recruitment and Retention Manager and the PDP Emerging Talent Recruitment Manager on ensuring our trial process is full adhered to with players attending on trial.

Individual Player Development

  • Deliver an individualised coaching programme that maximises every player's technical, tactical, physical and psychological development.

  • Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to ensure Individual Development Plans

  • are aligned across football, physical performance, psychology, education and medical services.

  • Monitor player progress through observation, objective performance data, analysis and regular player reviews.

  • Deliver position-specific coaching and specialist development sessions where appropriate.

  • Ensure every player understands their development objectives and takes ownership of their individual learning journey.

Collaboration & Football Integration

  • Work closely with the Youth Development Phase Manager to ensure alignment across all aspects of the Youth Development Phase curriculum.

  • Build a highly collaborative relationship with the Professional Development Phase Manager & Under 18 Head Coach to ensure continuity of coaching methodology, playing philosophy and transition planning.

  • Maintain strong communication with the Head of Academy and Head of Football Development to support succession planning and long-term player development across the Academy.

  • Support the wider Academy coaching programme by contributing across age groups where appropriate through but not limited to delivering sessions.

  • Build positive relationships across the multidisciplinary team to ensure players receive an integrated, holistic development programme.

  • Attend and contribute positively to Phase Meetings and multidisciplinary discussions as required.

  • Ensure players, parents and staff consistently uphold the Club's values and Codes of Conduct.

  • Create an environment where players take ownership of their development and embrace challenge as an opportunity to improve.

Administration & Compliance

  • Ensure all coaching administration, Individual Development Plans, Performance Clocks, player reports and YD Rules documentation are completed accurately and within required timescales.

  • Maintain compliance with Premier League, Football Association and Club policies, procedures and audit requirements being the lead on CASA for the Audit process.

  • Ensure all player records, educational documentation and development reports are maintained to the highest professional standards.

  • Undertake any additional duties reasonably requested by the Head of Academy or Head of Football Development.

  • Completes administration relevant to the job as required by the Head of Football Development and Head of Academy, meeting the requirements of the Premier League Youth Development rules and our own internal platforms.

What are we looking for:

Essential

  • UEFA A Licence.

  • FA Advanced Youth Award.

  • Demonstrable experience coaching in an elite Youth Development Phase.

  • Excellent understanding of long-term player development, a genuine youth developer and transition into senior football.

  • Outstanding knowledge of coaching methodology, player development and elite performance environments.

  • Excellent communication, organisation and presentation skills.

  • Ability to build collaborative relationships across football and multidisciplinary departments.

  • High-level IT, planning and performance analysis skills.

  • BFAS First Aid qualification.

  • Enhanced DBS clearance.

Desirable

  • UEFA Pro Licence (or working towards).

  • Professional playing experience.

  • Experience within a Category One Academy.

  • Additional qualifications in Sports Science, Performance Analysis, Psychology or Education.

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions or reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that may have been incurred. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed on a DBS disclosure if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements. Failure to satisfy the Club and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment.
job.plain_text_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application
Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week
Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR
Department: Academy Coaching
Reporting to: Youth Development Phase Manager
Closing Date For Applications: 10th August 2026
About the Role:
The Under 16 Head Coach is responsible for leading the coaching, performance and development programme for Nottingham Forest's Under 16 squad, creating an outstanding learning environment that prepares players for the successful transition into full-time football within the Professional Development Phase.
The post-holder will lead the planning, delivery and review of all aspects of the Under 16 football programme, ensuring coaching sessions, match preparation, fixtures and individual player development are fully aligned to the Club's coaching philosophy, playing identity and long-term player development strategy.
As the final age group within the Youth Development Phase, the role plays a critical part in preparing players for a scholarship programme and the demands of the Professional Development Phase. Working under the leadership of the Youth Development Phase Manager, the successful candidate will work in close collaboration with the Professional Development Phase Manager & Under 18 Head Coach to ensure every player's transition is planned, purposeful and centred around their individual development needs.
The role will also maintain a strong collaborative relationship with the Head of Football Development, ensuring player progression, succession planning and transition decisions remain aligned to the Academy's overall football strategy.
The successful candidate will create a demanding, innovative and player-centred environment that develops technically excellent, tactically intelligent and psychologically resilient players capable of thriving within Nottingham Forest's full-time development programme.
The Perks of the Job:
- Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground. - Employee Assistance Programme. - Access to high street and gym discounts. - Discount within our Club shop. - Free on-site parking.
Key Tasks and Responsibilities:
Under 16 Head Coach Responsibilities
- Lead and manage all aspects of the Under 16 football programme, ensuring the highest standards of coaching, preparation, performance and player development. - Plan, prepare, deliver and review all Under 16 training sessions, fixtures and competitive matches in line with the Club's coaching philosophy, playing identity and Academy methodology. Inclusive of training sessions on all three of our training models. - Create an innovative, demanding and enjoyable learning environment where players are challenged daily to maximise their long-term potential. - Develop players technically, tactically, physically, psychologically and socially in preparation for scholarship and full-time football. - Lead all Under 16 matchday activity, including squad selection, tactical preparation, in-game coaching and post-match review. - Embed the Academy's coaching methodology and playing principles into every aspect of the Under 16 programme. - Prepare players to meet the behavioural, physical, tactical and psychological expectations of the Professional Development Phase. - Foster professionalism, resilience, independence and accountability as players prepare to enter the next stage of the Academy pathway. - Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required by the Head of Academy, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy. - Ensure all information relating to the individual players performance clock and relevant team information is up to date daily on the Football iP platform. - Contribute to the Academy audit preparation ensuring all documentation is recorded and accurately keep up to date on a daily basis.
Player Development & Transition
- Take a leading role in preparing players for transition into the Professional Development Phase, ensuring every player is equipped to thrive within a full-time training environment. - Work closely with the Youth Development Phase Manager to review player progress, establish development priorities and agree appropriate player movement. - Develop an outstanding working relationship with the Professional Development Phase Manager & Under 18 Head Coach to ensure seamless transition of players into the Under 18 programme. - Collaboratively identify players who are ready to experience the Professional Development Phase through selected training sessions, fixtures and specialist development opportunities. - Contribute to scholarship recommendations, transition planning and succession planning across both phases. - Ensure all player movement between the Under 16s and Under 18s is supported by a clear developmental rationale and aligned to the player's Individual Development Plan. - Maintain regular dialogue with the Head of Football Development regarding players approaching scholarship, ensuring alignment with the Academy's long-term player pathway. - Liaise with the Head of Academy on recommendations for player scholarship offers through a strategic process of selection. - Assist the Youth Development Phase Recruitment and Retention Manager and the PDP Emerging Talent Recruitment Manager on ensuring our trial process is full adhered to with players attending on trial.
Individual Player Development
- Deliver an individualised coaching programme that maximises every player's technical, tactical, physical and psychological development. - Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to ensure Individual Development Plans - are aligned across football, physical performance, psychology, education and medical services. - Monitor player progress through observation, objective performance data, analysis and regular player reviews. - Deliver position-specific coaching and specialist development sessions where appropriate. - Ensure every player understands their development objectives and takes ownership of their individual learning journey.
Collaboration & Football Integration
- Work closely with the Youth Development Phase Manager to ensure alignment across all aspects of the Youth Development Phase curriculum. - Build a highly collaborative relationship with the Professional Development Phase Manager & Under 18 Head Coach to ensure continuity of coaching methodology, playing philosophy and transition planning. - Maintain strong communication with the Head of Academy and Head of Football Development to support succession planning and long-term player development across the Academy. - Support the wider Academy coaching programme by contributing across age groups where appropriate through but not limited to delivering sessions. - Build positive relationships across the multidisciplinary team to ensure players receive an integrated, holistic development programme. - Attend and contribute positively to Phase Meetings and multidisciplinary discussions as required. - Ensure players, parents and staff consistently uphold the Club's values and Codes of Conduct. - Create an environment where players take ownership of their development and embrace challenge as an opportunity to improve.
Administration & Compliance
- Ensure all coaching administration, Individual Development Plans, Performance Clocks, player reports and YD Rules documentation are completed accurately and within required timescales. - Maintain compliance with Premier League, Football Association and Club policies, procedures and audit requirements being the lead on CASA for the Audit process. - Ensure all player records, educational documentation and development reports are maintained to the highest professional standards. - Undertake any additional duties reasonably requested by the Head of Academy or Head of Football Development. - Completes administration relevant to the job as required by the Head of Football Development and Head of Academy, meeting the requirements of the Premier League Youth Development rules and our own internal platforms.
What are we looking for:
Essential
- UEFA A Licence. - FA Advanced Youth Award. - Demonstrable experience coaching in an elite Youth Development Phase. - Excellent understanding of long-term player development, a genuine youth developer and transition into senior football. - Outstanding knowledge of coaching methodology, player development and elite performance environments. - Excellent communication, organisation and presentation skills. - Ability to build collaborative relationships across football and multidisciplinary departments. - High-level IT, planning and performance analysis skills. - BFAS First Aid qualification. - Enhanced DBS clearance.
Desirable
- UEFA Pro Licence (or working towards). - Professional playing experience. - Experience within a Category One Academy. - Additional qualifications in Sports Science, Performance Analysis, Psychology or Education.
Forest For Everyone
We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.
Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.
Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.
Disability Confident Committed Employer
We are a Disability Confident Committed employer. We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.
If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to theEquality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via theDisability Confident Scheme- please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

job.title: Part-Time Associate, Growth Marketing
job.html_description:
JOB TITLE:  Part-time Associate, Growth Marketing  (30 hours per week)
REPORTING TO: Director, Growth Marketing
DEPARTMENT: Marketing        
LOCATION:  Manhattan
COMPENSATION: $20/hour, up to 30 hours per week 
 
POSITION OVERVIEW:  
The Part Time Associate, Growth Marketing role plays a pivotal part in expanding the club’s fan base and deepening engagement. This position supports data-driven marketing initiatives designed to attract new fans, convert interest into ticket sales, and strengthen long-term loyalty. This role will provide a unique experience to learn and assist in the creation of marketing campaigns across email, paid media, and CRM platforms. 

If you’re passionate about growing the beautiful game this is a perfect opportunity to join the Club at an exciting time with New York City’s first-ever soccer specific stadium on the horizon. The ideal candidate is proactive, curious, and thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. They bring both strategic thinking and hands-on execution to help the club reach new audiences and turn matchday moments into lifelong fandom. 
 
WHAT YOU’LL DO: 
  • Support the planning, execution, and optimization of fan acquisition and retention campaigns across digital channels. 
  • Manage campaign setup in collaboration with marketing, ticketing, and business intelligence teams. 
  • Assist in developing creative briefs, tracking performance metrics, and providing actionable insights for optimization. 
  • Monitor and analyze key growth KPIs 
  • Contribute ideas for new growth initiatives, testing opportunities, and ways to enhance the fan journey. 
  • Manage feedback and day to day maintenance of the club’s loyalty program  
  • Follow brand guideline and ensure quality communication to new and existing fans 
 
WHO YOU ARE: 
  • 1–3 years of marketing experience, ideally within sports, entertainment, or a high-growth consumer brand. 
  • Detail-oriented and capable of managing multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Proactive attitude, open to trying new ideas, eager to learn and highly organized 
  • Thrive in a collaborative environment 
  • Must have excellent communication skills  
  • Able to work independently, take initiative, and maintain a high level of professionalism within a professional sports environment 
  • Additional language/s is a plus. 
 
ADDITIONAL REQUIRMENTS: 
  • Applicant must be able to comply with MLS Next Safety and Well-Being policy and any other applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC 
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as necessary 

KEY RELATIONSHIPS 
  • Director, Growth Marketing 
  • Manager, Media Buying 
  • Manager, Lifecycle Marketing 
  • Senior Manager, Digital 
  • Cross functional departments – Ticketing, Partnership Marketing, Business Intelligence & Design 

WHAT WE OFFER: 
  • Two complimentary tickets to each home match 
  • Medical benefits through a third-party provider 
  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers  
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment  
 
NEW YORK CITY FC OVERVIEW: 
At New York City FC, we are on a mission to build this city into one of the soccer capitals of the world. The Club was announced as Major League Soccer’s 20th franchise and is the first and only MLS team located within the five boroughs of New York City. The Club has qualified for the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs nine times over the past 10 seasons, winning MLS Cup in 2021. Games are available to stream via an Apple TV subscription, providing every match of the MLS regular season, the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, annual Leagues Cup tournament, the MLS All-Star Game, the Campeones Cup, and more all in one place and with no blackouts. New York City FC is building New York City’s first-ever soccer-specific stadium, Etihad Park, which is set to open in 2027.

New York City FC is also one of 12 clubs comprising City Football Group and counts Manchester City FC, Melbourne City FC, Yokohama F-Marinos, Girona FC, Montevideo City Torque, Shenzhen Peng City FC, Lommel SK, ESTAC Troyes, Palermo FC, Bahia, and Club Bolívar among its sister clubs.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
  
By clicking "Apply Now", you agree to the terms of the MLS Privacy Policy.   
https://www.mlssoccer.com/legal/privacy-policy

job.title: Performance Analysis Intern
job.html_description:
JOB TITLE: Performance Analysis Intern
REPORTING TO: Academy Technical Director
DEPARTMENT: Sporting
LOCATION:  St. John’s University (Queens, NY) & CFA New York (Orangeburg, NY)
COMPENSATION: $17/hour, must be able to commit to working for the full duration of the Academy Season (August-May)
 
POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Performance Analysis Intern is responsible for supporting the delivery of performance analysis services within NYCFC’s Academy.
 
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
  • Training: film, code and database daily training sessions as requested.
  • Produce biweekly and monthly training reports.
  • Pre & Post Match: create and organize analysis’ support assets e.g. folder structures, reports templates, etc.
  • Match day: film and basic code Academy games when required
  • Contribute to the overall wider working and development of the Academy program
  • Ensure the operational requirements, such as uploading game footage to the correct platforms, are fulfilled as per deadline requirements. 
  • Attend all Academy, and other, meetings as requested. 
  • Other duties as assigned

WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
  • Must have good knowledge of soccer – either as former player, coach or similar. 
  • Must have proficient computer literacy skills and ability to assimilate new software and processes quickly
  • Familiarity with major Performance Analysis software (Sportscode, Match Analysis, Prozone, Hudl, Taka), Microsoft software (Excel, Powerpoint) and Mac software (Keynote, iBooks Author) strongly preferred
  • Familiarity and experience filming sporting events (ideally soccer) from a coaching perspective is preferred
  • Have flexibility to work differing hours on a weekly basis (including evening and weekends) – as agreed each week – depending on the game and schedule of First and Academy Team
  • Must be able to commit to working for the full duration of the Academy Season (August-May)
  • Ability to manage workload, set deadlines and priorities and utilize time management skills
  • Have an enthusiastic approach and proactive attitude
  • Must have excellent interpersonal and communication skills to effectively convey messages to colleagues, coaches and players
 
WHO YOU ARE:  
At New York FC, we are committed to upholding our core club values and our values guide how we show up and work together every day.  If you share our values listed below, please consider NYCFC as a great place for you to work (and play): 
Acts Honorably: listens and communicates respectfully, without judgement 
Engages Collaboratively: provides and seeks constructive feedback to and from peers, proactively sharing appreciation for quality contributions of others 
Champions Inclusion: celebrates the value of differences recognizing the value in the unique backgrounds and lived experiences of every team member 
Drives Forward: embraces new opportunities with curiosity and a focus on improvement and innovation 
Shows Heart: demonstrates passion for the Club and sport, operating as an NYCFC ambassador in encouraging and inspiring that passion in others 

ADDITIONAL REQUIRMENTS:
  • Applicant must be able to comply with applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as necessary
  • Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times   

 WHAT WE OFFER:
  • Two complimentary tickets to select New York City FC home match
  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment

job.title: Per Diem Academy Athletic Trainer, Part-Time
job.html_description:
JOB TITLE: Per Diem Academy Athletic Trainer, Part-Time
REPORTING TO: Head of Performance Services
DEPARTMENT: Sporting, Academy
LOCATION: St John’s University, Queens College, City Football Academy-Orangeburg
COMPENSATION: $50-65 per hour, commensurate with experience and qualifications. 5-25 hours per week.

POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Part-Time Academy Athletic Trainer (AT) supports the daily sports medicine operations for NYCFC Academy teams by providing medical coverage for trainings, matches, tournaments, and club events. This role is responsible for supporting injury prevention sessions, emergency care, injury evaluation, treatment, and assisting with the delivery of high-quality medical services that support player health and long-term athlete development.

Working closely with the full-time medical and performance staff, the Part-Time Academy Athletic Trainer helps deliver a safe, professional, and player-centered environment while supporting the development of the next generation of NYCFC players.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:
  • Provide athletic training coverage for Academy training, matches, tournaments, and special events.
  • Perform emergency care, first aid and immediate injury management.
  • Deliver treatment and recovery interventions within scope of practice.
  • Collaborate with Performance staff to support player health, recovery, and testing batteries.
  • Represent NYCFC professionally and contribute to a positive, player-centered environment.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
  • Certified Athletic Trainer (ATC) with an active New York State License.
  • BOC Certified and member in good standing with NATA (or CATA).
  • Current CPR/AED and First Aid certification.
  • Minimum 1 year of experience in sports medicine preferred.
  • Experience working with soccer and/or youth or high-performance athletes preferred.
  • Strong communication and organizational skills.
  • Bilingual (Spanish) is a plus.
  • Professional liability insurance required.

WHO YOU ARE:  
At New York FC, we are committed to upholding our core club values and our values guide how we show up and work together every day.  If you share our values listed below, please consider NYCFC as a great place for you to work (and play): 
 
Acts Honorably: listens and communicates respectfully, without judgement 
Engages Collaboratively: provides and seeks constructive feedback to and from peers, proactively sharing appreciation for quality contributions of others 
Champions Inclusion: celebrates the value of differences recognizing the value in the unique backgrounds and lived experiences of every team member 
Drives Forward: embraces new opportunities with curiosity and a focus on improvement and innovation 
Shows Heart: demonstrates passion for the Club and sport, operating as an NYCFC ambassador in encouraging and inspiring that passion in others 

ADDITIONAL REQUIRMENTS:
  • Applicant must be able to comply with applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as necessary
  • Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times

  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers 
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment

job.html_description:
JOB TITLE: Academy Athletic Trainer
REPORTING TO: Head of Performance Services, Academy
DEPARTMENT: Sporting, Academy
LOCATION:  St John's University, Queens / City Football Academy, Orangeburg

POSITION OVERVIEW:
New York City FC is seeking an Academy Athletic Trainer (AT). This role plays a vital role in the daily sports medicine operations for NYCFC’s Academy teams. This individual will oversee injury prevention, emergency care, injury evaluation, player treatment, and health administration [DH2.1]for Academy players, to support holistic performance development. The Academy AT will collaborate closely with the Lead Academy AT and Head of Performance Services to deliver top-tier care and performance programming aligned with the club’s methodology and long-term athlete development goals.

This is a dynamic role that blends hands-on athletic training, data-informed performance support, and collaboration across departments to help guide and develop NYCFC’s next generation of professional players.  It is through the Academy pathway that our First Team develops Homegrown talent, ensuring a strong and vibrant future while embodying the club's identity and values.  The successful candidate will align with these values and understand that they are role models for our players on and off the pitch.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Medical & Athletic Training Duties
  • Serve as an Athletic Trainer for NYCFC Academy teams during trainings and/or matches (Home and Away)
  • Provide medical services including injury assessment, emergency care, and ongoing treatment
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date medical records using our athlete management system
  • Coordinate medical referrals and collaborate with physicians as needed
  • Manage medical inventory and ensure clinical equipment is in working order
Performance & Interdisciplinary Collaboration
  • Partner with Performance staff to deliver comprehensive athlete development, including:
    • Strength and conditioning support
    • Warm-up routines and mobility programs
    • Load management and recovery strategies
    • Nutrition and hydration education
    • Data monitoring 
  • Assist with fitness assessments, training periodization, and preseason/offseason planning.
  • Actively communicate with technical staff, players, and families to align care plans and progress.
Additional Contributions
  • Participate in NYCFC’s Youth Affiliate Education initiatives.
  • Contribute to a positive and collaborative environment within the Academy and wider NYCFC organization.
  • Work closely with NYCFC II and First Team departments to ensure continuity in care and long-term player development.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING: 
  • Certified Athletic Trainer (ATC) with an active NY State License.
  • Member in good standing with NATA (or CATA); NATABOC certified.
  • Minimum 1-2 years of professional experience in sports medicine (preferably with youth or high-performance athletes).
  • Current CPR and emergency care certification.
  • Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) preferred.
  • Previous experience in soccer and/or with youth athletes is highly desirable.
  • Bilingual (Spanish) a plus.
  • Must hold personal professional liability insurance.

Shows Heart: demonstrates passion for the Club and sport, operating as an NYCFC ambassador in encouraging and inspiring that passion in others

  • Applicants must be able to comply with MLS Next Safety and Well-Being policy and any other applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC
  • Willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and travel for matches and camps.

COMPENSATION:
This exempt position has an estimated annual base salary of $62,355 and is not overtime eligible. Final compensation offer amounts are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to demonstrated skill set, years and depth of relevant experience, and some role-dependent factors such as certifications and software expertise. We welcome direct conversations with each candidate about compensation in all of our initial calls.

  • Two complimentary tickets to every NYCFC home match 
  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers 
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment

job.title: Foundation Phase Academy Coach
job.html_description:
JOB TITLE:  Foundation Phase Academy Coach
REPORTING TO:  Academy Technical Director
DEPARTMENT: Sporting
LOCATION:   St. Johns University; Queens & City Football Academy :Orangeburg, New York 
 
POSITION OVERVIEW:
As an Academy Coach you will have the overall responsibility in the continued development of a specific age group. You will be responsible for the delivery of the NYCFC coaching philosophy and managing Individual Development Plans for the players. You will lead the interdisciplinary team in achieving individual and team goals. It is important that you are willing and able to work together across departments and other age groups. You will be responsible for the development program of the team and individuals, working in a multidisciplinary environment. This role will be based in the Foundation Phase. 
 
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
  • Create a learning environment that balances challenges and support for each individual player.
  • Maximize the potential of every player through the delivery of the NYCFC game model and methodology.
  • Deliver the content of all daily training sessions and match preparation, together with your staff.
  • Work cooperatively with other Academy teams and staff and maintain relationships with appropriate internal and external stakeholders.
  • Plan, deliver, and review coaching practices according to the NYCFC methodology, with an action-oriented attitude and a commitment to continual improvement.
  • Work from a periodization model and conduct practice designs to enhance the learning and understanding of NYCFC's game model.
  • Work with other Academy coaches to deliver one-to-one player development support through progressive Individual Development Plans, providing ongoing, specific, and actionable feedback.
  • Understand and adhere to all Competition Guidelines in all entered competitions.
  • Represent NYCFC in a positive manner while carrying out all required responsibilities.
  • Support the continued development and matriculation of Academy players to progress through our system.
  • Engage with, and ensure timely input into, all Academy platforms and software (Smartabase, Taka, etc.).

WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
  • 5+ experience coaching youth academy level.
  • USSF ‘B or A’ license – minimum (required) 
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work multidisciplinary in the context of Soccer. 
  • Valid driver’s license 
  • Knowledge of Microsoft office; PowerPoint, Word, and Excel
  • Knowledge of tactical periodization and how to implement it.
  • A growth mindset and willingness to join the team with enthusiasm and curiosity. 
 
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
  • Applicant must be able to comply with MLS Next Safety and Well-Being policy and any other applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC
  • Must be able to work games scheduled which may be at night and on weekends and holidays

COMPENSATION:
This exempt position has an estimated annual base salary range of $62,500-65,000. Final compensation offer amounts are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to demonstrated skill set, years and depth of relevant experience, and some role-dependent factors such as certifications and software expertise. We welcome direct conversations with each candidate about compensation in all of our initial calls.
 
WHAT WE OFFER:
  • Excellent health, dental & vision insurance, with options to fit you and your family’s needs
  • Comprehensive and competitive benefit programs, including maternal & paternal leave
  • Ancillary benefits: Commuter, gym membership, and Citi Bike discounts
  • Your health is important! Our wellness strategy focuses on mental and physical wellbeing through in-office and virtual programs
  • Four complementary tickets to every NYCFC home match
  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment

job.title: Academy Goalkeeper Coach (Part-Time)
job.html_description:
JOB TITLE:  Academy Goalkeeper Coach (Part-Time)
DEPARTMENT:  Academy
REPORTING TO: Academy Technical Director
LOCATION:  St. John’s University (Queens, NY) & CFA New York (Orangeburg, NY)
COMPENSATION: $30-35/hour, 15 hours per week

POSITION OVERVIEW:
New York City FC is seeking a dedicated and experienced Goalkeeper Coach to join our Academy staff. Working with our U12-18 age groups, you will be responsible for supporting the development of all of our Academy goalkeepers. This role will demand a high level of off-field expertise as well as a very strong ability to design, plan, and execute on-field sessions and build individual development plans while ensuring alignment with the overarching philosophy and playing style of NYCFC and City Football Group. This role will play a pivotal part in the development of goalkeepers within our academy, fostering their technical, tactical, physical, psychological, and social growth. Finally – you will also be part of the City select and scouting & recruitment of the new Goalkeepers for our incoming U12 team and any other team within the academy. Expect ad hoc requests for travelling days domestic and internationally.

WHO YOU ARE: 
At New York FC, we are committed to upholding our core club values and our values guide how we show up and work together every day.  If you share our values listed below, please consider NYCFC as a great place for you to work (and play):
 Acts Honorably: listens and communicates respectfully, without judgement
Engages Collaboratively: provides and seeks constructive feedback to and from peers, proactively sharing appreciation for quality contributions of others
Champions Inclusion: celebrates the value of differences recognizing the value in the unique backgrounds and lived experiences of every team member
Drives Forward: embraces new opportunities with curiosity and a focus on improvement and innovation
Shows Heart: demonstrates passion for the Club and sport, operating as an NYCFC ambassador in encouraging and inspiring that passion in others

WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Training and Development 
  • Design, plan and deliver daily goalkeeper-specific training sessions according to the clubs Game Model and Methodology.
  • Support the creation of a curriculum for the U12-18 goalkeepers in accordance with the playing style and principles of NYCFC.
  • Supporting the assessment of all U12-U18 GK’s in the Academy and provide detailed feedback to both staff and the players/parents. 
  • Utilize video analysis and modern coaching tools to enhance goalkeeper development and performance
  • Ensure that every Academy goalkeeper has a clear Individual Development Plan (IDP). 
  • Aid in on goalkeeper scouting/ recruitment within the Academy. This will include supporting the planning and delivery of goalkeeper try-outs, clinics and camps as well as attending local and nationwide events.
Matchday Responsibilities
  • Delivering to the U12-U18 Goalkeepers during matches and tournaments, including warm-ups and pre-game strategies for them.
  • Support the head coaches and technical staff in match preparation when requested
  • Provide in-game observations and adjustments to ensure goalkeeper development and performance.
Collaboration and Integration
  • Work closely with the NYCFC Academy Goalkeeper Coach and attend/deliver as per his instruction.
  • If requested, assist the first and second team goalkeeper coaches to ensure continuity and alignment in goalkeeper development.
  • Collaborate with the strength and conditioning team to design fitness programs tailored to goalkeeper needs.
  • Coordinate with performance coaches and medical staff on load management and injury prevention.
Administration and reporting
  • Maintain detailed records of goalkeeper performance, training attendance, and progress.
  • Provide regular progress reports to the Acdaemy Technical Director as requested.
  • Attend staff meetings, logistics meetings and other events as required by the club.
  • Complete all administration associated with the NYCFC Academy platforms (Kitman, Hudl, TAKA etc).
 
WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
  • 3-5 years of youth goalkeeper coaching background/experience
  • Strong teaching background
  • Dual language English/Spanish is preferred
  • Knowledge and know-how of Microsoft office
  • Drivers license 
  • Strength in delivering tactically relevant on-field sessions
  • Hold a relevant coaching license (e.g., UEFA B License, USSF B License, or equivalent) or a goalkeeper-specific coaching license is highly preferred
  • Proven experience as a goalkeeper coach at the professional, collegiate, or elite youth level.
  • Experience in combining practical on-field know how with off-field planning and assessment
  • Ability to communicate effectively with players, staff, and other stakeholders.
  • Passionate about player development with a commitment to NYCFC's values and philosophy.
  • Collaboration with fellow coaches with a multidisciplinary approach
  • A motivated growth mindset and life-long learner
  • Strong work ethic
  • Competency in using analysis software particularly Hudl/Sportscode
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.

ADDITIONAL REQUIRMENTS:
Applicant must be able to comply with applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC
Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as necessary
Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times   

WHAT WE OFFER:
  • Two complimentary tickets to select New York City FC home match
  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment

JOB TITLE: Academy Goalkeeper Coach (Part-Time)
DEPARTMENT:Academy
REPORTING TO: Academy Technical Director
LOCATION:St. John’s University (Queens, NY) & CFA New York (Orangeburg, NY) COMPENSATION:$30-35/hour, 15 hours per week
POSITION OVERVIEW:
New York City FC is seeking a dedicated and experienced Goalkeeper Coach to join our Academy staff. Working with our U12-18 age groups, you will be responsible for supporting the development of all of our Academy goalkeepers. This role will demand a high level of off-field expertise as well as a very strong ability to design, plan, and execute on-field sessions and build individual development plans while ensuring alignment with the overarching philosophy and playing style of NYCFC and City Football Group. This role will play a pivotal part in the development of goalkeepers within our academy, fostering their technical, tactical, physical, psychological, and social growth. Finally – you will also be part of the City select and scouting & recruitment of the new Goalkeepers for our incoming U12 team and any other team within the academy. Expect ad hoc requests for travelling days domestic and internationally.
WHO YOU ARE:
At New York FC, we are committed to upholding our core club values and our values guide how we show up and work together every day. If you share our values listed below, please consider NYCFC as a great place for you to work (and play):
Acts Honorably: listens and communicates respectfully, without judgement
Engages Collaboratively: provides and seeks constructive feedback to and from peers, proactively sharing appreciation for quality contributions of others
Champions Inclusion: celebrates the value of differences recognizing the value in the unique backgrounds and lived experiences of every team member
Drives Forward: embraces new opportunities with curiosity and a focus on improvement and innovation
Shows Heart: demonstrates passion for the Club and sport, operating as an NYCFC ambassador in encouraging and inspiring that passion in others
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Training and Development
- Design, plan and deliver daily goalkeeper-specific training sessions according to the clubs Game Model and Methodology. - Support the creation of a curriculum for the U12-18 goalkeepers in accordance with the playing style and principles of NYCFC. - Supporting the assessment of all U12-U18 GK’s in the Academy and provide detailed feedback to both staff and the players/parents. - Utilize video analysis and modern coaching tools to enhance goalkeeper development and performance - Ensure that every Academy goalkeeper has a clear Individual Development Plan (IDP). - Aid in on goalkeeper scouting/ recruitment within the Academy. This will include supporting the planning and delivery of goalkeeper try-outs, clinics and camps as well as attending local and nationwide events.
Matchday Responsibilities
- Delivering to the U12-U18 Goalkeepers during matches and tournaments, including warm-ups and pre-game strategies for them. - Support the head coaches and technical staff in match preparation when requested - Provide in-game observations and adjustments to ensure goalkeeper development and performance.
Collaboration and Integration
- Work closely with the NYCFC Academy Goalkeeper Coach and attend/deliver as per his instruction. - If requested, assist the first and second team goalkeeper coaches to ensure continuity and alignment in goalkeeper development. - Collaborate with the strength and conditioning team to design fitness programs tailored to goalkeeper needs. - Coordinate with performance coaches and medical staff on load management and injury prevention.
Administration and reporting
- Maintain detailed records of goalkeeper performance, training attendance, and progress. - Provide regular progress reports to the Acdaemy Technical Director as requested. - Attend staff meetings, logistics meetings and other events as required by the club. - Complete all administration associated with the NYCFC Academy platforms (Kitman, Hudl, TAKA etc).
WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
- 3-5 years of youth goalkeeper coaching background/experience - Strong teaching background - Dual language English/Spanish is preferred - Knowledge and know-how of Microsoft office - Drivers license - Strength in delivering tactically relevant on-field sessions - Hold a relevant coaching license (e.g., UEFA B License, USSF B License, or equivalent) or a goalkeeper-specific coaching license is highly preferred - Proven experience as a goalkeeper coach at the professional, collegiate, or elite youth level. - Experience in combining practical on-field know how with off-field planning and assessment - Ability to communicate effectively with players, staff, and other stakeholders. - Passionate about player development with a commitment to NYCFC's values and philosophy. - Collaboration with fellow coaches with a multidisciplinary approach - A motivated growth mindset and life-long learner - Strong work ethic - Competency in using analysis software particularly Hudl/Sportscode - Strong organizational and time-management skills.

job.title: Training Facilities - Security Guard, OHP
job.html_description:
TITLE: Security Guard, Training Facility

DEPARTMENT:  Training Facilities 
REPORTS TO: Security Manager 

FLSA: Part Time, Hourly; Non-Exempt 
 

WHAT SETS YOU APART

We are looking for an honest, attentive, and perceptive individual to join our Security team. You will be responsible for securing the Orlando Health Training Facility at Osceola Heritage Park and protecting the Club’s property, guests, staff, and players. You ensure safety while promoting and enforcing security and act as a visible deterrent against irregular activity. 

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Patrol the Orlando Health Training Facility at Osceola Heritage Park property to monitor and prevent intrusion, damage, hazards and breaches of security.   
  • Lock and unlock doors and walk facilities. 
  • Provide a visible presence that enforces safety and security 
  • Monitor activity throughout the facilities via closed circuit television. 
  • Respond appropriately to emergencies that arise including, but not limited to, fire alarm and burglar alarm. 
  • Monitor access to the facility.  
  • Assist with Event Day security coverage.
  • Detect and confront unauthorized persons and violators of security procedures. 
  • Contact relevant authorities to deal with unlawful or irregular activities. 
  • Use radio or other communication devices in a clear and concise manner 
  • Write reports, report any malfunctions, misconduct or operational and safety issues. 
  • Interview victims and witnesses and write incident reports as necessary. 
  • Maintain a professional appearance and attitude.  
  • Implement the prescribed emergency plan in case of emergency 
  • Assist with the development and implementation of public safety plans for day-to-day operations and special events. 
  • Other duties as assigned.  

 

QUALIFICATIONS 

It’s never just a job at Orlando City SC.  It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer and entertainment. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications:

  • Must possess a High School diploma or G.E.D. or equivalent. 
  • Some college studies in Criminal Justice, Private Investigations, Homeland Security, Emergency Management, Emergency Medical Services and/or any other Security related field or military experience is preferred. 
  • Six (6) months to one (1) year security experience preferably in a similar environment 
  • Bilingual in Spanish or Portuguese is preferred. 
  • Excellent aptitude to establish rapport with others and ability to build strong interpersonal relationships. 
  • Basic computer skills including Microsoft Office suite. 
  • Ability to pass a criminal background check and employment verification. 
  • Must have a valid FL driver license and Class D Security License.  
  • The ability to attain and maintain Safesport certification.
  • Appropriate credentials as mandated by State, County or local law. 
  • Ability to work independently with little or no supervision. 

  

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Must be able to move and/or lift up to 50 pounds. 
  • Must be able to walk, run, kneel and climb stair and react fast to unpredictable situations. 
  • This position requires work inside and outside of the building and some exposure to adverse conditions. 
  • Prolonged periods of sitting, and monitoring surveillance equipment.   


About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride: 

 

In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut.  

The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons. 

In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win.  

The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year.

 

In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando.

 

In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League.  

For more information on Orlando City SC and Orlando, visit OrlandoCitySC.com or Orlando-Pride.com.

 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

 

Orlando City and Orlando Pride will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation(s) to participate in the job application or interview process and perform critical job functions. Please contact the People and Culture department at Peopleandculture@orlandocitysc.com to let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

job.title: Team Operations - Academy Team Administrator
job.html_description:
TITLE: Team Administrator – Academy
DEPARTMENT: Team Operations
REPORTS TO: Head of Academy Operations
FLSA: Full-time; Exempt

 

WHAT SETS YOU APART

The Team Administrator will provide comprehensive administrative and operational support across the Academy’s Pre-Formation and Formation age groups. This role will work closely with the Head of Academy Operations, Director of Soccer Operations, and Academy Director.  This role will be an integral piece ensuring smooth day-to-day delivery of Academy programming in alignment with MLS standards, Orlando City SC operational expectations, and safeguarding requirements.

 

The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented, with experience supporting elite youth soccer environments. This individual will serve as a central point of coordination for players, parents, coaches, and external stakeholders while ensuring all operational, registration, scheduling, travel, and compliance processes are delivered to a high professional standard.

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

 

  • Provide full administrative and operational support for all Pre-Formation and Formation age groups across training, fixtures, tournaments, showcases, and special events.
  • Coordinate and maintain all phase-specific schedules, calendars, and communications through Teamworks and other club communication platforms.
  • Serve as a primary administrative contact for players, parents, coaches, and support staff within assigned age groups.
  • Assist with the day-to-day operational delivery of academy programming in accordance with MLS standards and club policies.
  • Maintain accurate academy records, player files, attendance tracking, registration documentation, and operational reports.
  • Support the Head of Academy Operations with academy-wide operational projects and initiatives.
  • Support the organization and execution of MLS events, tournaments, festivals, friendlies, and showcase competitions.
  • Coordinate communication with internal departments, including facilities, groundskeeping, security, and medical staff, to ensure operational readiness.
  • Assist with all player registration processes through MLS, U.S. Soccer, and applicable federation systems.
  • Support compliance with MLS roster regulations, player movement policies, safeguarding standards, and competition requirements.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of MLS rules, academy standards, and youth player compliance procedures.
  • Assist with international clearance and player documentation processes where applicable.
  • Coordinate team travel arrangements for assigned academy teams in collaboration with the Head of Academy Ops and Finance. 
  • Maintain consistent and professional communication with players and families regarding schedules, travel, programming updates, and operational information.
  • Promote a positive and professional experience that reflects the values and standards of Orlando City SC.
  • Coordinate Academy player housing logistics, including host family placements, housing documentation, onboarding, monitoring, and conclusion of host family agreements in accordance with club policies.
  • All other duties as assigned.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

 

It’s never just a job at Orlando City SC. It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Sports Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Minimum 2–4 years of experience in team operations, Academy administration, or elite youth sports environments preferred.
  • Previous experience working within MLS academies, professional academies, collegiate athletics, or elite youth soccer environments preferred.
  • Knowledge and understanding of MLS rules, youth player registration processes, and Academy operational standards preferred.
  • Experience coordinating logistics, including fixtures, tournaments, travel, and events.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and athlete management platforms such as Teamworks.
  • Strong organizational, administrative, and multitasking skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to interact effectively with players, parents, coaches, and staff.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Flexible schedule with availability to work evenings, weekends, and travel domestically as required.
  • Bilingual in Spanish or Portuguese preferred but not required.
  • Ability to pass a background screening.
  • Ability to attain and maintain SafeSport certification.

 



About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride: 

 

In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut.  

The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons. 

In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win.  

The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year.

 

In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando.

 

In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League.

job.html_description:
TITLE:  Sports Turf Specialist, Stadium

DEPARTMENT:  Stadium Operations 
REPORTS TO:  Grounds Supervisor

FLSA:  Full-time Hourly; Non-Exempt 

  

WHAT SETS YOU APART  

Are you a self-motivated individual with physical stamina? Do you love the outdoors and maintaining aesthetically pleasing outdoor space? If so, our Sports Turf Specialist role could be for you. You will be responsible for mowing, fertilization, edging, irrigation troubleshooting and repair, top dressing, aerating, painting, sodding, and record keeping for the Inter.co Stadium. You will get a chance to use a variety of practical skills which are valuable and essential to the overall Club.   

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:  

  • Assist with all operations of field maintenance at Inter.co Stadium to include painting, mowing, irrigation, aerification, chemical application and any special projects as needed 
  • Proactively identify turf grass diseases, weeds, pests, and work with Director of Turf & Grounds and Grounds Supervisor to take corrective action as needed 
  • Assist in equipment and irrigation repair and maintenance 
  • Work MLS games, NWSL games and third party events based on business needs 
  • Create and maintain good working relationships with all MLS and NWSL coaches and soccer operations staff 
  • Participate in procuring equipment and supplies as needed for the facility 
  • Provide coverage at the training facilities as needed 
  • Other duties as assigned 

   

QUALIFICATIONS  

It’s never just a job at Orlando City SC and Orlando Pride.  It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer and entertainment. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications:  

  • Bachelor’s degree in Turf Grass Science, Horticulture, or related field preferred. 
  • 1-3 years of grounds maintenance related work experience in soccer 
  • Candidate should possess or have the ability to obtain the Florida Commercial Pesticide Applicator License. 
  • Ability to operate turf related equipment (i.e., tractors, mowers, aerifiers, field paint machine). 
  • Possess excellent written/verbal communication skills, be detail-oriented and highly organized with the ability to simultaneously handle multiple tasks and adapt to change. 
  • Ability to resolve concerns expeditiously and independently. 
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.). 
  • Fluency in Spanish is preferred but not required. 
  • Experience with hosting field events including sporting and concerts, using various field protection systems is a plus. 
  • Ability to perform physical labor for extended periods of time and in various weather conditions. 
  • Able to work flexible hours including nights, weekends, and holidays. 
  • Ability to walk and stand for short periods of time. 
  • The ability to attain and maintain Safesport certification. 
  • The ability to pass a background screening.

In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win.  

The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. job.title: Team Operations - Academy Strength and Conditioning Coach
job.html_description:
TITLE: Academy Strength & Conditioning Coach

DEPARTMENT: Team Operations

REPORTS TO: Academy Head of Strength & Conditioning

FLSA: Salary; Exempt

 

WHAT SETS YOU APART

The Academy Strength and Conditioning Coach provides assigned Academy players with high-level, age-appropriate performance training and education. The coach applies scientific and practical knowledge to support player development, improve performance, and reduce injury risk.  Responsibilities include planning, delivering, and monitoring strength and conditioning programs for assigned teams; conducting soccer-specific physical testing; supporting recovery and return-to-performance processes; and providing sport science support. The role operates with day-to-day autonomy for assigned teams, within the methodology, standards, and supervision established by the Academy Head of Strength & Conditioning, and collaborates with the multidisciplinary department (Athletic Training, Sports Science, Nutrition, and Technical Staff).

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Work collaboratively with all department members and under the direction of the Academy Head of Strength & Conditioning.
  • Plan, design, and implement safe, effective, and age-appropriate strength and conditioning programs for assigned Formation players, in accordance with the Academy methodology.
  • Lead and deliver sports performance training sessions independently for assigned teams.
  • Develop daily, weekly, and monthly training plans for assigned teams, aligned with the technical and tactical schedule and reviewed by the Academy Head of Strength & Conditioning.
  • Coordinate with coaching staff to integrate physical development objectives into the plans of assigned teams.
  • Educate and counsel Players regarding age-appropriate strategies to improve performance, recovery, and professional habits.
  • Communicate with sports medicine staff regarding injured, rehabilitating, and deconditioned Players, and modify programs with agreement from the medical staff.
  • Contribute to the design and implementation of return-to-performance strength and conditioning programs under the direction and agreement of medical and performance leadership.
  • Conduct Player performance testing according to established Academy protocols and assist with the interpretation and communication of results.
  • Collect, organize, analyze, and report strength, conditioning, and performance data for assigned teams.
  • Manage training and match tracking data for assigned teams within established departmental systems and data-collection structures.
  • Identify relevant performance trends and communicate practical observations and recommendations to the Academy Head of Strength & Conditioning and multidisciplinary staff.
  • Provide operational support, coverage, and informal guidance to less-experienced Academy Strength & Conditioning staff when requested, without formal line-management responsibility.
  • Maintain the appearance, safe functionality, and organization of equipment in the weight facility, and educate and enforce weight room rules.
  • Demonstrate the interpersonal and communication skills required to work effectively with Players, coaches, Club personnel, and Academy staff.
  • Attend activities, meetings, matches, and programs as required by Academy leadership.
  • Other duties as assigned.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

It’s never just a job at Orlando City.  It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Strength & Conditioning, Sports Science, Applied Kinesiology, or a related field.
  • CSCS (NSCA) or PES (NASM) preferred but not required.
  • CPR certification required (or obtain within 30 days of hire).
  • Ability to attain and maintain SafeSport certification.
  • Ability to pass a background check.
  • Bilingual (English, Spanish, or Portuguese) preferred but not required.
  • Effective academic and applied knowledge of contemporary practice in performance training, strength development, rehabilitation support, and youth athlete development.
  • Proven experience working with soccer academy or junior athletes.
  • Experience with movement, speed, strength, and power training appropriate for developing athletes.
  • Experience with physical testing, workload monitoring, and basic performance-data analysis.
  • Proficient in PowerPoint, Excel, and Word.
  • Minimum of 3 years of previous soccer strength and conditioning or physical performance experience required.
  • Experience independently supporting one or more teams or age groups preferred.
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends.

 



About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride: 

 

In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut.  

The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons. 

In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win.  

The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year.

 

In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando.

 

In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League.  

For more information on Orlando City SC and Orlando, visit OrlandoCitySC.com or Orlando-Pride.com.

 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

 

Orlando City and Orlando Pride will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation(s) to participate in the job application or interview process and perform critical job functions. Please contact the People and Culture department at Peopleandculture@orlandocitysc.com to let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.
